annotations.title: Settled, linked and delivered, across the rails

description: BEFORE YOU QUOTE ANY FIGURE FOR AGENT COMMERCE, ask which of three it is. Every payment shown to be one, x402 and ACP, is split into three figures that NEST and are never added up (x402 counts only the `protocol`, `route` and `facilitator` tiers below; the authorised transfers with nothing to show they were x402 are in `notShownToBeX402`, never in the figures): `settled` (paid on-chain), of that `serviceLinked` (paid to a payee that lists a paid service, or an ACP job), of that `deliveryEvidenced` (a recorded outcome: an ACP job completed). x402 records the payment and never the delivery, so its payments are counted in `deliveryUnevidenceable`: $0 delivered there is what the rail allows, not a failure of the seller. Beside it, `tiers` splits x402 payments by what can be shown about the payment itself: to a listed route, through a facilitator, or only an authorised transfer. Free, because it is an aggregate; the same split for one address is on agent_business.

commerceTiers.description: `settled`, `serviceLinked`, `deliveryEvidenced` and `deliveryUnevidenceable`, each {count, usd}; `rails` per rail; `says` in one line; `limits`; `asOf` when the daily rollup ran. NULL until it has run, never a row of zeros.

tiers.description: x402 payments by what can be shown about them: `route`, `facilitator`, `candidate`, `candidate-unsampled`, each with payments and usd. No tier is protocol-confirmed: the HTTP 402 receipt never reaches a chain.
